title: Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 vs 9950X3D vs 9850X3D: Who Needs Two V-Cache Dies?
summary: The Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 puts V-Cache on both chiplets. Here's how it compares with the 9950X3D, 9850X3D, 9800X3D and 9950X, and who should buy it.
body_markdown:
AMD's Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 Dual Edition went on sale on April 22, 2026, and it answered a question enthusiasts had been asking for years: what if both of a 16-core Ryzen's chiplets got 3D V-Cache? The launch reviews have had time to settle, and the answer is more interesting than "it's faster."


Using the launch reviews, I've compared it with the four chips people actually cross-shop it with. My conclusion, up front: it's an excellent processor for a narrow group of people, and the wrong one for nearly everyone who games.


## The Contenders


All five are Zen 5, socket AM5 and ship without a cooler.


- **Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 Dual Edition:** 16 cores with V-Cache stacked under both chiplets.
- **Ryzen 9 9950X3D:** 16 cores with V-Cache on one chiplet.
- **Ryzen 7 9850X3D:** 8 cores, one chiplet with V-Cache, higher boost than the 9800X3D.
- **Ryzen 7 9800X3D:** the 8-core gaming chip that started this generation.
- **Ryzen 9 9950X:** 16 cores, no V-Cache.


## Side-by-Side Specs


CPU Cores / Threads Max Boost L3 Cache TDP


Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 16 / 32 5.6GHz 192MB 200W


Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16 / 32 5.7GHz 128MB 170W


Ryzen 7 9850X3D 8 / 16 5.6GHz 96MB 120W


Ryzen 7 9800X3D 8 / 16 5.2GHz 96MB 120W


Ryzen 9 9950X 16 / 32 5.7GHz 64MB 170W


## Deep Dive


### Ryzen 9 9950X3D2: Brilliant at Simulation, Pointless for Gaming


The[Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 Dual Edition](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16819113938?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_ryzen-9-9950x3d2-vs-9950x3d-vs-9850x3d) carries 192MB of L3 cache, 64MB stacked under each chiplet, with a 200W TDP. Because both chiplets now behave the same way, HotHardware noted that AMD's 3D V-Cache core-parking driver no longer needs to steer games onto the "right" chiplet. That's a real quality-of-life improvement.


Performance is where expectations need managing. Tom's Hardware found "little to no advantage in games, and even slight regressions in some titles," and TechSpot's 14-game average landed at essentially the same level as the 9950X3D. On Windows productivity work, gains over the 9950X3D were small: TechSpot measured about 7 percent in Blender, and Tom's Hardware saw roughly 4 percent in multithreaded tests overall.


Then Phoronix ran more than 300 Linux benchmarks and found a 10 percent geometric-mean lead over both the 9950X and 9950X3D, with gains of 20 percent or more in OpenFOAM CFD, several scientific simulation codes, PostgreSQL and Whisper.cpp. That's the audience: people whose workloads live in cache, often on Linux. The cost is power. TechSpot measured 27 percent more CPU power draw for a 4 percent gain in its multithreaded Cinebench test, and a peak of 89°C on a 360mm AIO. AMD's own page recommends liquid cooling, so I'd pair it with something like the[MSI MAG CoreLiquid A13 360](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16835846069?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_ryzen-9-9950x3d2-vs-9950x3d-vs-9850x3d) .


### Ryzen 9 9950X3D: The One Most Creators Should Buy


The[Ryzen 9 9950X3D](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16819113884?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_ryzen-9-9950x3d2-vs-9950x3d-vs-9850x3d) gives you 16 cores, 128MB of L3 and gaming performance that matches the X3D2 in TechSpot's testing, at a 170W TDP. For people who game and render, it's the more sensible 16-core chip. Club386 put it this way: the 9950X3D "will serve most creators' needs at considerably less expense."


### Ryzen 7 9850X3D and 9800X3D: Still the Gaming Choices


For a gaming PC, I'd still point you to the 8-core chips. The[Ryzen 7 9850X3D](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16819113934?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_ryzen-9-9950x3d2-vs-9950x3d-vs-9850x3d) boosts to 5.6GHz against the 5.2GHz of the[Ryzen 7 9800X3D](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16819113877?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_ryzen-9-9950x3d2-vs-9950x3d-vs-9850x3d) , both with 96MB of L3 and a 120W TDP. Tom's Hardware put the 9850X3D ahead of the X3D2 for gaming, and TechSpot found Rainbow Six Siege ran 4 percent slower on the X3D2 than on the 9800X3D.


### Ryzen 9 9950X: Still a Strong Workstation Value


The[Ryzen 9 9950X](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16819113841?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_ryzen-9-9950x3d2-vs-9950x3d-vs-9850x3d) has only 64MB of L3, but if your work is rendering and encoding rather than cache-sensitive simulation, it remains a capable 16-core chip. The X3D2's biggest lead over it came in Phoronix's Linux suite.


## Building Around a 16-Core X3D


Existing AM5 boards should work after a BIOS update, so check your board's support list first. For a new build, a board with solid power delivery like the[MSI MAG X870E TOMAHAWK WIFI](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16813144699?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_ryzen-9-9950x3d2-vs-9950x3d-vs-9850x3d) makes sense, and if your work needs it, two 32GB sticks like the[G.SKILL Trident Z5 Neo 64GB DDR5-6000 CL30](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16820374443?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_ryzen-9-9950x3d2-vs-9950x3d-vs-9850x3d) kit. AMD rates two-DIMM setups higher than four, so I'd stick with two sticks.


## Winner by Category


- **Gaming:** Ryzen 7 9850X3D, with the 9800X3D close behind.
- **Gaming plus content creation:** Ryzen 9 9950X3D.
- **Linux simulation, CFD and cache-heavy compute:** Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 Dual Edition.
- **Rendering on a tighter budget:** Ryzen 9 9950X.


Tom's Hardware summed it up well: of 100 builders, they'd steer 99 to another chip. If you're the hundredth, you probably already know it.


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Is the Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 good for gaming?** It's fast, but not faster than cheaper X3D chips. Tom's Hardware found little to no gaming advantage and slight regressions in some titles, and TechSpot measured essentially the same gaming performance as the Ryzen 9 9950X3D.


**What is the difference between the 9950X3D2 and the 9950X3D?** The 9950X3D2 Dual Edition stacks 3D V-Cache under both chiplets for 192MB of L3 cache and has a 200W TDP. The 9950X3D has V-Cache on one chiplet, 128MB of L3, a 5.7GHz max boost and a 170W TDP.


**Who should buy the Ryzen 9 9950X3D2?** People running cache-sensitive work such as CFD, scientific simulation and some database workloads, especially on Linux. Phoronix measured a 10 percent geometric-mean lead over the 9950X and 9950X3D across more than 300 tests, with 20 percent-plus gains in several simulation codes.


**Does the 9950X3D2 still need AMD's core-parking driver?** Not for steering games. HotHardware reports that because both chiplets have V-Cache and behave similarly, the optimizer's chiplet-steering layer is no longer necessary.


**What cooler does the Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 need?** It ships without a cooler, and AMD recommends liquid cooling. TechSpot recorded 89 degrees Celsius under all-core load on a 360mm AIO, so a 360mm liquid cooler is a sensible choice.
